submitted.rationale: Index 8 (Pb 0.52) sits at the Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore composition. MACE puts that phase on the hull and MEGNet gives it an HSE gap of about 2.5 eV, below the 3.2 eV illumination. Its EQE of 0.0263% was the highest measured, about 35–60x the other two compositions. EQE drops steeply on both sides of it, so the maximum is sharp and sits at this phase.

rejected.reason: PbSb2O6-rich region: measured EQE was only 0.00045%, even though the predicted gap is 2.7 eV
Pb-rich mix of pyrochlore and PbO: measured EQE was 0.00074%, and PbO's gap of about 3.36 eV is above the 3.2 eV photon energy

consultations.verdict: Support: Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore (Pb 0.5) is on hull per MACE and has HSE gap ~2.5 eV, below the 3.2 eV photon energy, so near-phase-pure film at index 8 (Pb 0.52) should absorb and is the leading candidate. PbSb2O6 (gap 2.7, stable) near index 13 is the second candidate.

Supportive by contrast: PbO (litharge) HSE gap 3.36 eV exceeds 3.2 eV illumination, so the Pb-rich end probably absorbs weakly unless Pb3O4 (0.95 eV, likely a recombination-prone mixed phase) forms. That makes the Sb-rich PbSb2O6 (stable, gap 2.7 eV from earlier) region near index 13 the best untested option after the pyrochlore at index 8.

Mildly supportive: PbO is on the hull (MACE), so Pb-rich films past index 8 should be a stable mix of the pyrochlore Pb2Sb2O7 (2.5 eV gap, absorbing) and PbO. EQE rose about 60x from Pb 0.34 to Pb 0.52, which points toward the Pb-rich side. Index 5 (Pb 0.63) keeps a lot of the absorbing pyrochlore while testing that trend, and it is also the GP-UCB pick.
